children: Fed's modernization efforts will ensure that the discount window supports individual banking institutions and broader market resilience, according to the Federal Reserve Board Governor Philip Jefferson.

The Fed's discount window lending program provides liquidity to banks. Banks access discount window liquidity overwhelmingly through primary credit borrowing, which is offered on a "no questions asked" basis.
Jefferson was speaking before the 2026 Treasury Markets Conference hosted by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.
He listed certain modernization efforts that the Fed was undertaking to make discount window borrowing faster and less operationally burdensome.
First, ongoing business process improvements have been supporting better efficiency and standardization.
Second, there have been enhancements made to the discount window user experience.
Third, collaboration with the FHLBs, which are important liquidity providers to banking organizations.

"These improvements, I believe, help reduce the frictions that may make banks hesitant to use the window when they are healthy and reinforce overall confidence in the banking system," said the Fed governor.

"The U.S. Treasury market serves as the foundation for pricing risk across all asset classes, facilitating the efficient allocation of capital throughout our economy. In this context, the discount window supports Treasury market resilience in important ways. By providing banks with a reliable source of liquidity, the discount window serves as a shock absorber during periods of market stress by reducing the risk of forced sales of Treasury securities," said Jefferson.

"By alleviating funding pressures at depository institutions, the discount window helps ensure the smooth functioning of key short-term funding markets—including the repurchase agreement market and the federal funds market. This dynamic, in turn, supports Treasury market liquidity," he said.
